clauses.text:
By virtue of the authority vested in 
me by the Civil Service Act (22 Stat. 403) 
and by section 1753 of the Revised Stat­
utes of the United States, and as Presi­
dent of the United States, it is ordered 
that Executive Order No. 9721 of May 
10, 1946, authorizing the transfer, under 
certain conditions, of civilian employees
13 CFR, 1944 Supp. 
*  3 CFR, 1946 Supp.
in the Executive branch of the Federal 
Government to public international or­
ganizations in which the United States 
Government participates, be, and it is 
hereby, amended in the following re­
spects :

1. Section 1  is amended, effective as of 
May 10,1946, by adding at the end there­
of the following sentence:'
“Any employee so transferred shall, 
for a period not to exceed three years 
from the date of transfer and while em­
ployed by the said international organ­
ization, be considered as being on leave 
of absence from his employment by the 
Federal Government: Provided, that the 
employee is subsequently reemployed by 
the Federal Government in accordance 
with section 3 of this order.”

2. Section 2, which by its terms be­
came inoperative on May 10, 1949, is re­
vived and amended, effective as of that 
date, to read as follows:
“Any employee serving under a war- 
service indefinite appointment who is 
transferred to a public international or­
ganization pursuant to this order and, 
while serving in such organization and 
within three years from the date of such 
transfer, is either reached in regular 
order for probational appointment from 
a civil-service register appropriate for 
filling the position in which he was serv­
ing or could, with the approval of the 
head of such agency, have been given a > 
competitive status under Civil Service 
Rule III if he had remained in the posi­
tion in which he last served in a Federal 
agency, shall be considered as having 
acquired a competitive status as of the 
date he is reached, for probational 
appointment or classification. Any em­
ployee transferred to a public interna­
tional organization pursuant to this order 
who was serving in such organization on 
September 30, 1949, and had served con­
tinuously therein from the date of his 
transfer shall be considered, so far as 
Executive Order No. 10080 or September 
30,1949,* is concerned, as having been in 
an active-duty status on September 30, 
1949, in the position in the Federal Gov­
ernment from which he was transferred 
and as having had continuous service 
with the Federal Government from the 
date of his transfer to September 30, 
1949.”

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10103 (15 FR 597; govinfo PDF text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), headed Executive Order 10103, Amendment of Executive Order No. 9721 of May 10, 1946, Providing for the Transfer of Personnel to Certain Public International Organizations, signed February 1, 1950. Inventory: the enacting paragraph and two numbered amendments (1, adding the three-year leave-of-absence sentence to section 1; 2, reviving and amending section 2 on competitive status, including the sentence about Executive Order 10080), recorded as three clauses; the held page also prints neighbouring orders, which are outside the inventory. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 revokes the numbered orders in its table, and any amendments thereto; the table lists both 9721 and 10103 (subject: amending provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations), and the U.S. Code note at 22 U.S.C. 288 note records that the orders were revoked with certain savings by section 2 of Executive Order 10804 and subsequently revoked by Executive Order 12553. The enacting provision of 12553 has no stated effective date, so it is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. Earlier partial revocation: section 2 of Executive Order 10804 (signed 1959-02-12, 24 FR 1147) revokes 9721 and 10103 insofar as they affect employees covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957, except that each remains in effect for an employee serving with an international organization on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act who does not elect coverage under that Act and for rights and benefits vested before that date. Because the revocation is qualified by those exceptions, it does not extinguish the commands for the saved class and is recorded as a later event, not as the first end. Later waivers for named individuals (Executive Order 11138 of 1964-01-07 and Executive Order 11303 of 1966-09-12) are later events on the leave-of-absence sentence, not ends. Searches: the OFR executive-order catalog search and the USC and eCFR citation searches were selected after reading their coverage notes (complete; no coverage warning; the USC edition runs through 2026-10-09 and the eCFR search to 2026-10-14, which cannot matter for an order whose end is shown in 1986 or earlier).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Candidate earlier ends examined. (1) Section 2 of Executive Order 10804 (1959-02-12): an express revocation, but only insofar as the orders affect employees covered by section 6(a) of the International Atomic Energy Agency Participation Act of 1957, and expressly not for non-electing employees serving on the date of enactment of the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act or for vested rights; the saved class and vested rights keep the commands in force, so the revocation is partial and is recorded as a later event with its exceptions. Evidence decides: no source shows the commands extinguished for every person before 1986. (2) Executive Orders 11138 and 11303 waive time limits for named individuals; they amend how the order applies and do not end it. (3) The statute Federal Employees International Organization Service Act (72 Stat. 961) is not held, so no statutory replacement is claimed as an end. EO 12553 is the first held instrument that revokes the orders without exception.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: clause 1 (leave of absence for up to three years while employed by the international organization, if reemployed under section 3) and clause 2 (competitive status for certain transferred war-service employees, and the sentence treating certain employees as in active-duty status for Executive Order 10080) are separate amendments of Executive Order 9721 but each is an amendment of the same parent order, shares the parent's end, and none has its own sunset shown in held evidence. Under the strike-and-insert ruling of 2026-10-21 each continues, amended, until the parent ends.","savings_check":"Savings and residual effects: accrued leave-of-absence status, reemployment rights and competitive status survive as accrued effects (state transferred_or_accrued); Executive Order 10804 saves vested rights; the Executive Order 12553 enacting provision has no exception.","scope_check":"Scope: the dossier leads target provision not located: EO:10080, EO:11138 and EO:11303 are resolved. Executive Order 10080's held text does not mention 10103 or 9721 (10103 mentions 10080, not the reverse), so 10080 acts on nothing here. Executive Orders 11138 and 11303 each modify Executive Order 9721 as amended by 10103 by waiving a time limit for one named person; the leave-of-absence limit in section 1 is the sentence added by clause 1 of this order, so they are recorded as later events on clause 1, and neither revokes anything. Executive Order 11138 also waives the section 3(a) reemployment limit, which is in 9721's own text and not in this order's inventory."}

savings_residuals.reason: Leave-of-absence status, reemployment rights and competitive status that employees acquired under the order are accrued effects; Executive Order 10804 itself saves rights and benefits vested before the Federal Employees International Organization Service Act, and the enacting provision of Executive Order 12553 has no savings clause. No held source shows a continuing independent command of the order after 1986-02-25.
